title: Wear-IT Study Specification
description: This specification contains all the needed information to both run a study using the Wear-IT framework. This includes all the needed information to make reproducible and replicable codebooks for complex designs.

examples.Study.Name: Recovery Community Center Project
examples.authors: Jane Smith, John Doe, Emily R. Johnson
examples.abstract: This study examined daily stress and recovery patterns among adults attending a recovery community center. Participants completed ecological momentary assessments four times daily over 14 days across two bursts.

Study.Name.description: Human readable long name for a study

authors.description: String of all people to be credited for this study. This will appear in the authors section of a generated codebook.

funding.description: String containing relevant funding info for the study

abstract.description: String containing qualitative description of the study. This could include main study objectives, relevant findings, study population etc.

ai_generation.title: AI Generation Metadata
ai_generation.description: Metadata indicating whether this study specification was generated (fully or partially) by an AI tool.

ai_generated.description: Whether this study spec was generated by an AI tool.

tool.description: Name and version of the AI tool or model used to generate this spec (e.g. 'WearIT-GPT v1.2', 'claude-sonnet-4-20250514').

generated_at.description: ISO 8601 timestamp of when this spec was generated.

burst.title: Burst Specifications
burst.description: An object of named burst specifications. Each key is a free-form researcher-chosen burst name (e.g. 'baseline', 'intervention', 'follow_up'). Each burst represents a distinct repeating data collection block.

description.description: Optional human-readable description of this burst (e.g. 'Baseline 14-day collection period').

survey.title: Survey Specifications
survey.description: An object of named survey specifications within this burst. Each key is a free-form researcher-chosen survey name. Each survey represents a distinct instrument delivered to participants.

schedule.title: Schedule
schedule.description: Defines when and how this survey is delivered. Separated from the survey content to keep scheduling concerns distinct. A schedule specifies the overall delivery period, within which windows define daily opportunity periods, and cadences define how often prompts fire within those windows.

Timing.Type.description: Type of timing governing this schedule. Discrete = equal time distance; Random = random sample from a time period; Triggered = rule-based; Continuous = uneven time intervals.

window.title: Window
window.description: The daily opportunity period during which a participant may receive a prompt. For example, a window from 6am to 10am means the app may only deliver surveys within that 4-hour block. Defines the outer boundary of availability.

start.description: Start time of the daily window in HH:MM (24h) local time (e.g. '06:00').

end.description: End time of the daily window in HH:MM (24h) local time (e.g. '22:00').

length.description: Duration of the window as a value+unit pair. Can be derived from start/end but may also be specified directly.

cadence.title: Cadence
cadence.description: Defines the rhythm of prompts fired within the window. Answers 'how often does the app prompt the participant during the window?' For example, every 30 minutes, or 4 random prompts across the window.

repeat.title: Repeat
repeat.description: How many times the prompt fires within the window per day. For a fixed cadence this may be derived (window / interval). For random cadences this sets the explicit count.

count.description: Number of prompts to deliver within the window.

random.description: If true, the repeat.count prompts are placed randomly within the window rather than at fixed intervals.

timing.title: Timing
timing.description: Low-level offset/interval values used to define the spacing between prompts within the window. Used when cadence is fixed (Discrete). For example, an offset of 30 minutes means prompts fire every 30 min from window start.

children.description: Nested timing levels for complex recursive schedules.

Trigger.Info.description: Optional trigger logic. Used when cadence is Triggered rather than Discrete or Random.

Conditional.Source.description: Source of measurement to trigger conditional.

Conditional.Threshold.description: Preset value being compared to the participant response.

question.title: Question Specification
question.description: Contains all the information needed to specify a question or variable in a survey, observation, or passive data collection context.

examples.Question.Long.Name: Perceived Stress Item 1
examples.Question.Text: How stressed have you felt in the past hour?
examples.Question.Description: A self-report measure of perceived stress on a scale from 0 (not at all) to 100 (extremely).
examples.Question.Type.Display.Name: Slider

Question.ID.description: Name of the variable as it appears in the dataset

Question.Long.Name.description: Human readable name for the variable

Question.Text.description: Exact text of the question as presented to the participant. Only applicable for survey questions.

Question.Description.description: Description of the variable in layman's terms. If layman's terms are not possible, provide a citation to a longer explanation.

Question.Type.Display.Name.description: How the data was obtained. Must match one of the supported Wear-IT display types.

examples.definition: Less than five minutes (just stopped in)

definition.description: Human-readable label for the response value.

Parent.description: Item ID of the parent item. NOTE: This is different from the conditional master which points to the item which, if successful, delivers the current item. Parent may point to a block many questions up.

Conditional.Info.description: Contains all the conditional info for a question

Conditional.Child.Item.ID.description: Item ID for the successful child of the current question.

Conditional.Fail.Item.ID.description: Item ID for the fail child of the current question.

Conditional.Master.Item.ID.description: Item ID for the parent of the current question.

Conditional.Threshold.description: Threshold is the preset value being compared to the user response.

Data.Type.description: The type of data captured by this variable.

dataSets.title: Data Sets Specification (Column Vector Format)
dataSets.description: Renamed from 'data'. All fields are stored as column vectors (arrays), where each position corresponds to a participant/record in the dataset.

Alert.Times.description: Each entry is a participant-level array of alert times.

itemMap.title: Item Map Repo
itemMap.description: This specification contains all the needed information to describe a single item or scale used within the Wear-IT framework, including its conceptual, psychometric, and delivery properties.

examples.Item.Text: How stressed did you feel today?
examples.Modeling.Characteristics: Typically used as an outcome variable; no transformation required
examples.Scale.Name: Perceived Stress Scale
examples.Top.Level.Question: Indicate to what extent you...
examples.Definition: Never, Almost Never, Sometimes, Fairly Often, Very Often
examples.Article.Title: A global measure of perceived stress
examples.Citation: Cohen, S., Kamarck, T., & Mermelstein, R. (1983). https://doi.org/10.2307/2136404
examples.notes: Standard PSS-10 item; time stem adapted from original

Item.Text.description: Exact text of the item as presented.

Conceptualization.description: What construct or concept does this item measure or represent?

Modeling.Characteristics.description: Usual modeling characteristics or how this item is typically used in analysis.

Validated.description: Whether this item is part of a statistically validated measure.

Scale.Name.description: Name of the scale this item belongs to.

Parent.Scale.description: Name of the parent scale if this item belongs to a subscale.

Sub.Scale.description: Name of the subscale this item belongs to, if applicable.

scaleOrItem.description: Whether this entry represents a full scale or a single item.

Scale.Type.description: The type of scale this item uses (e.g. Likert, VAS, semantic differential, binary, forced choice).

Scoring.description: How this item or scale is scored.

Reverse.Coded.description: Whether this item is reverse coded.

Transformation.description: Description of any transformation applied beyond simple reverse coding.

Identifying.Info.description: Whether this item potentially contains personally identifying information.

Data.Type.description: Type of data this item produces.

Time.Stem.description: The time reference embedded in the item.

Top.Level.Question.description: The top-level or parent question this item falls under.

Definition.description: Nominal or text-based response options or categories.

Delivery.Mechanism.description: How the item is delivered to the participant.

Delivery.Frequency.description: How frequently this item is delivered.

Citation.description: DOI citation or APA formatted citation for the item or scale source.

notes.description: Any additional notes about this item.
